subject.title: fix(release): stop npm lock fork packaging loops

question: Does the release owner accept preserving all multi-version pnpm forks as parent-scoped npm-lock entries rather than applying any same-line global version override?
rationale: This is a deliberate release-packaging resolution policy change with an observed npm 11 failure mode; source-level correctness is supported by the focused patch and proof, but the permanent package-resolution policy belongs to the release owner.

options.title: Accept the fork-preserving policy
options.body: Merge the patch with the supplied Slack packaging evidence and retain the regression test as the contract.

options.title: Require broader package fixtures
options.body: Keep the PR open until additional representative multi-version package graphs demonstrate that parent-scoped overrides remain npm-installable.

recommendation.title: Accept the fork-preserving policy
recommendation.body: Merge the patch with the supplied Slack packaging evidence and retain the regression test as the contract.

likelyOwner.reason: The PR author is the active release-packaging contributor and supplied the concrete failing and passing package evidence.
